makemeahanzi.definition: to argue, to dispute; to discuss, to debate

etymology.hint: A bitter 辛 exchange of words 讠

characterDeckComponents.note: 讠 (speech, words) — the middle of the character, an exchange of talk.
辛 (bitter, sharp), placed on both sides, representing the two disputing parties, together giving 辩 its meaning 'to argue, debate.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to omit; to remove; to withdraw

etymology.hint: A guard dog 犭 talking 讠 to a prisoner 犬

characterDeckComponents.note: 犭 (dog) on the left represents a guard dog.
讠 (speech) suggests an accusation or a legal case being spoken.
犬 (dog) on the right completes the scene, giving 狱 its meaning 'prison, lawsuit.'

meanings: cable (unit of length: 100 fathoms, about 185 m)
chain (unit of length: 66 feet, about 20 m)

etymology.hint: Metal 钅 that joins 连; 连 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 钅 (metal) marks the material — links and chains are typically made of metal.
连 (to connect) sits beside it — metal pieces connected together, giving 链 its meaning 'chain.'

makemeahanzi.definition: deadline; period; measure word for elections, meetings, and other events

characterDeckComponents.note: 舟 (boat) — 舰 names a large military ship.
见 (jiàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 舰.

makemeahanzi.definition: to help, to aid, to assist

characterDeckComponents.note: 力 (strength) — 助 relates to helping, lending one's strength
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound connection to 助's reading zhù
宀 (roof) — 宽 originally described a spacious house.
苋 (xiàn) gives a sound distantly related to kuān, having drifted apart over time.

etymology.hint: A man with head 日 and hands 共 tormenting a deer 水

characterDeckComponents.note: 日 here pictures a person's head.
共 pictures two hands; together with the shape below, they depict a violent struggle, giving 暴 its meaning 'violent, sudden.'
女 (woman) — 婆 names an older woman.
波 (bō) gives a sound close to pó, sharing the same rhyme.

makemeahanzi.definition: certain, sure; definite, exact; real, true

characterDeckComponents.note: 石 (stone) — 确 originally meant firm and solid like stone, extending to 'true, accurate, indeed.'
角 (jiǎo) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from què.
兔 depicts a rabbit's body with long ears and a short tail, seen in profile.

meanings: to sweep (with a brush or broom)

makemeahanzi.definition: to clean, to sweep, to wipe away; to weed out; to wipe out

etymology.hint: Simplified form of 掃; to use 扌 a broom 帚; 帚 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 (hand) — 扫 describes using the hand to sweep.
帚 depicts a hand-held broom — held by the hand 扌, it gave 扫 its meaning 'to sweep.'
犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú

makemeahanzi.definition: to lay out, to place, to set aside

characterDeckComponents.note: 罒 (a net) — 置 originally meant to set a net in place
直 (zhí) gives a sound close to 置's reading zhì, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
彡 (fine lines, streaks) — 彩 relates to patterns and bright colors.
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — an exact match with 彩's reading cǎi.

etymology.hint: A flat 枼 stone 石

characterDeckComponents.note: 石 (stone) — early dishes were sometimes made of or associated with stone/ceramic material.
枼 depicts something flat and thin, giving 碟 its meaning 'a small, flat dish.'

meanings: to break (a stick, a bone etc)
(bound form) to sustain a loss (in business)

makemeahanzi.definition: to break, to snap; to fold, to bend; to bow; humble

etymology.hint: A hand 扌 wielding an axe 斤

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 (hand) does the action.
斤 (axe) — chopping and snapping something in two gives 折 its meaning 'to break, to bend.'
米 (grain) — 粗 originally described coarsely hulled grain, extending to 'rough, coarse' in general.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to cū's reading, having drifted apart considerably over time.

makemeahanzi.definition: cover, shroud; basket for catching fish

characterDeckComponents.note: 罒 (net) — 罩 originally described a net-like cover or trap.
卓 (zhuó) gives a sound close in initial to zhào, though the rhyme has drifted over time.

etymology.hint: Two objects 口 strung 丨 together

characterDeckComponents.note: Represents an object, repeated twice, that is threaded together.
A vertical line running through, like a string.
⺮ (bamboo) — 箭 names an arrow, traditionally made from a bamboo shaft.
前 (qián) shares the rhyme -ian with jiàn, though the initial has drifted from q- to j- over time.
口 (mouth) — 嚼 describes chewing, an action of the mouth.
爵 (jué) gives the sound — an exact match with 嚼.

makemeahanzi.definition: cluster of flowers; earlobe; an item on both sides

etymology.hint: Flowers 几 blooming on a tree 木

characterDeckComponents.note: 木 (tree) at the bottom is the plant the flowers grow from.
几 above represents a blossom or cluster of flowers atop the tree, giving 朵 its use as a classifier for flowers and clouds.

etymology.hint: A formation 阝of soldiers 车

characterDeckComponents.note: 阝 (a mound/formation) — soldiers arranged in position
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in formation

makemeahanzi.definition: to stop, to rest, to lodge; constellation

etymology.hint: A person 亻 sleeping in a bed 百 under a roof 宀

characterDeckComponents.note: Roof — shows shelter, a place to stay.
A person resting inside, suggesting lodging for the night.
自 (originally a picture of a nose) — 鼻 names the nose.
畀 (bì) gives a sound close to bí, differing only in tone.

etymology.hint: Costing little 戋 money 贝; 戋 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 贝 (currency, wealth) sits on the left.
戋 means 'small, little' — paired with money 贝, this pictures something costing very little, giving 贱 its meaning 'cheap, of low value.'

etymology.hint: A hand with a dot indicating where the pulse can be felt, about an inch up the wrist

characterDeckComponents.note: 寸 pictures a hand with a small mark near the wrist, showing the point about an inch up where a pulse can be felt — the image behind its meaning 'inch, small.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to show, to prove, to make known

characterDeckComponents.note: 艹 (plant) — the original meaning of 著 related to plants standing out or being placed
者 (zhě) gives a sound close to one reading of 著, zhù; the common grammatical reading 'zhe' used here carries no stress and no clear tie to that sound

makemeahanzi.definition: to be defeated, to collapse, to fail

characterDeckComponents.note: 土 (earth) — 垮 describes something collapsing to the ground.
夸 (kuā) gives a sound close to kuǎ, the same syllable with a different tone.
忄 (heart) shows 慌 relates to an emotional state.
荒 (huāng) gives the exact sound of 慌.

makemeahanzi.definition: to hold, to choke; to gather in one hand

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 is the semantic element, tying the character's meaning to the hand.
臽 (xiàn)'s own standalone reading is obscure today, so its exact historical closeness to "qiā" is hard to verify with confidence.

makemeahanzi.definition: millstone; to grind, to polish, to rub, to wear out

characterDeckComponents.note: 石 (stone) — 磨 names a millstone, or the act of grinding with one.
麻 (má) shares the initial m- and tone with mó, though the rhyme has drifted slightly from á to ó.

makemeahanzi.definition: to establish, to create; cut, wound, trauma

characterDeckComponents.note: 刂 (a knife) — 创 relates to cutting or wounding, extended to mean 'to start, to create,' as a fresh cut marks a new beginning
仓 (cāng) gives a loose sound connection to 创's reading chuàng

meanings: to mark with a symbol, label, lettering etc
to bear (a brand name, registration number etc)

characterDeckComponents.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo

meanings: general term for a bird of prey

characterDeckComponents.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鹰 names a bird of prey, the falcon or eagle.

makemeahanzi.definition: to pour, to spill; to scatter, to shed; to wipe away

characterDeckComponents.note: 氵 (water) — 洒 describes scattering or spilling liquid.
西 (xī) gives a sound only distantly related to sǎ today, having drifted apart over time.

makemeahanzi.definition: to prepare; to get ready, to equip; ready; perfect

etymology.hint: To go 夂 to the farm 田 to prepare for a harvest

characterDeckComponents.note: 夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'
隹 (short-tailed bird) — 雅 originally named a type of crow, later borrowed for the unrelated meaning 'elegant, refined.'
牙 (yá) gives a sound close to yǎ, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.

etymology.hint: An animal with horns 丷, eyes 田, nose 一, and mouth 口

characterDeckComponents.note: 丷 (horns) at the top shows the animal's horns.
田 (here shaped like a head with eyes) in the middle represents the animal's face.
口 (mouth) at the bottom completes the creature's face, giving 兽 its meaning 'beast, animal.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to open, to unfold; to extend, to stretch

etymology.hint: Laying out clothes 㠭 for sale in a market 尸; compare 㠭

characterDeckComponents.note: 尸 (here representing a covering or stall, not a corpse) — 展 pictures a place where goods are displayed.
衣 (clothing) — clothing laid out for display gave 展 its meaning 'to unfold' or 'to exhibit.'
钅 (metal) reflects the character's old sense tied to metal goods laid out for display in a shop, the source of 铺's meaning "shop."
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound distantly related to pù, having drifted apart over time.

makemeahanzi.definition: to decrease, to subtract, to diminish

characterDeckComponents.note: 冫 (ice) — melting ice shrinks away, an image linked to 减's meaning 'to decrease.'
咸 (xián) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading jiǎn has diverged.
辶 (to walk) shows 逊 relates to an action or manner, here yielding humbly.
孙 (sūn) gives a sound distantly related to xùn, having drifted apart over time.
页 (head) — 额 names the forehead, part of the head.
客 (kè) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading é has diverged considerably.
扌 (hand) — 挪 describes moving something by hand.
那 (nà) gives a sound close to nuó, sharing the same initial.
